input.summary: Dawn in the Golden Company's camp outside Volantis. Marro straps Rickard's armor; Hesse reports the watch on the Black Wall doubled and six elephants in the yard below the Triarch's tower, and the Triarch's grain cart two days late. Hesse privately asks Marro to meet her alone at the picket by the old well after the noon meal. A man in Pallo's grey loiters in camp, watching Marro and then the commander's tent.

updates.body: The Triarch's watch on the Black Wall is doubled at the east gate and the river stair, and six elephants now stand in the yard below the Triarch's tower (none the day before).
The Triarch's grain cart to the Golden Company camp is two days late.
Rickard's shoulder wound bled through its bandage overnight; he refuses the surgeon and leaves off the left pauldron.
A man in Pallo's grey has come into the Golden Company camp, loitering at the horse lines and the cook fires, watching Marro and the commander's tent.
Hesse asked Marro to meet her alone at the picket by the old well after the noon meal, and to tell her what Pallo's man wants with him.

input.summary: Late at night in Rickard's tent, Marro brings him the last of the Lyseni wine and hones his cudgel's iron cap with the old whetstone. Rickard, drunk and in pain, talks of wanting land and of doing what you must to get it, and says his knighthood promise stands only if the city falls. After Rickard sleeps, Marro silently searches the tent: nothing from the Triarch in the open, only the locked strongbox at the foot of the cot, whose key hangs on a knotted cord at Rickard's neck. The scene ends with Marro beside the sleeping captain, the key within reach.

updates.body: Marro's cudgel has a folded iron cap; he hones its edges with Rickard's old whetstone, which Rickard told him to keep whatever happens.
By Golden Company law, a captain can dub as knight any man who has earned it in the field.
Rickard told Marro the knighthood promise holds only if the company is over the Wall by summer; 'Cities don't always fall.' He spoke of wanting land and doing what you have to to get there.

Marro searched Rickard's tent while he slept, unnoticed. He found nothing from the Triarch in the open, and saw that Rickard keeps a locked strongbox at the foot of his cot, its key on a knotted cord at his neck. Marro does not know what is in the strongbox. The dispatch satchel holds a grain tally that has been made to add up.
The company's wine is gone: Rickard drank the last of the Lyseni.

thread_changes.body: Rickard spoke of the Triarch as 'he' and of doing what you must for land. Marro has seen the locked strongbox and the key at Rickard's neck.

thread_changes.title: The strongbox
thread_changes.body: Rickard's iron-banded strongbox, key on a cord at his neck. Marro has not opened it.
